title: Coded Segment
description: A single segment of a coded interview. The basic unit of analysis. Produced by `09-flat-coding`, read by all downstream analysis skills.

segment_id.description: Unique segment ID within an interview. Format seg-NNNN (4 digits). Numbering runs continuously through the interview.

respondent_id.description: Respondent ID: R01, R02, ..., R100. Corresponds to the card in `3-analysis/respondents/<ID>.md`.

speaker.description: Who is speaking in the segment. `interviewer` segments are kept for context but are not used as evidence.

timecode_start.description: Start of the segment in the source recording, format HH:MM:SS.

timecode_end.description: End of the segment, format HH:MM:SS.

verbatim.description: Verbatim text of the segment. MUST exist in the source transcript character-for-character. Checked by the verbatim validator before writing.

content_type.description: Epistemic status of the segment. fact — what the respondent did, observed, or experienced (behavior and experience). interpretation — their explanation of why. hypothesis — their guess about the future or about causes they are themselves unsure of. Used downstream when selecting quotes and phrasing findings; not printed into final artifacts.

content_codes.description: Flat codes close to the respondent's words. No hierarchy. Verb or noun phrases, not categories. Grouping is the job of `13-axial-coding`.

research_question_ids.description: Which research questions this segment addresses. Empty array = segment is on the research topic but does not directly answer any research question. Non-empty does not mean evidence — only relevance.

hypothesis_support.description: Link between the segment and the hypotheses from `project-config.yaml`. Empty array or absent — the segment is evidence neither for nor against.

direction.description: confirm — the segment is evidence for. disconfirm — against. nuance — refines the boundaries of applicability.

confidence.description: The coder's confidence that this particular segment was coded correctly (not in the truthfulness of the respondent's words). low — needs a second pair of eyes or more context.

notes.description: Internal coder notes. They do not appear in the output artifacts for the researcher.
